dispatch.headline: Guild Card Arrives. Farmer Was Home.
dispatch.body:
The Gene-Editing Guild's card of apology reached the far hemisphere's only tardigrade-farmer on the 1,094th day of travel. It is the longest delivery in colony records.

Two thousand engineers set out. 1,962 arrived. Seven were lost to the Salt Divide, and 31 stayed behind to keep the road home open.

The Guild built 14 walking crawlers to carry the card. Three finished the trip. The Guild also packed 400 spare copies in case of damage. Of those, 396 were damaged.

The card has six printed words: "Sorry we missed you. Please rebook."

The Guild's own survey drones logged the farmer at home 212 times when the Guild first called. Nobody knocked once.

The expedition leader gave a 41-minute farewell speech at the farmer's gate. The farmer replied with one word. It was not recorded.

The farm holds 9,000 tardigrade tubs. The engineers were asked not to step in any of them. They stepped in 1,310.

A Guild spokesperson was heard on the cost: "He ordered one vial in the first year, and nobody came, so we came."

The farmer has since rebooked. The Guild says the next slot is in three years.
dispatch.scene: A lone weathered farmer in a patched coverall stands at a wooden gate, holding a small white card at arm's length, while a vast column of helmeted engineers with crawler machines stretches across the dusty plain behind him.

glossary.gloss: a farmer who raises tardigrades, tiny water bears, in tubs
walking machines built to carry loads over rough ground

dispatch.premise: The colony's gene-editing guild sends a three-year expedition to the far hemisphere to deliver a 'Sorry We Missed You' card to a lone hermit tardigrade-farmer, ceremonially escorted by two thousand engineers.

drafts.headline: Revived Colonist Finishes Orientation, Fire Exit Now A Hill
drafts.body:
A colonist revived after nine hundred years finished six weeks of Welcome Back orientation on Friday, having covered the lanyard, the icebreaker and the fire-exit map of a building that is now a hill. Results of the final attendance count follow.

Sessions attended by the colonist: 42 of 42.

Lanyards issued: 1. Lanyards worn by facilitators: 4.

Icebreaker rounds completed: 11. Facts about self offered by the colonist: 3, all about the building.

Exits on the map: 6. Exits still above ground: 0.

Exits that could be found by digging: 2, per the hill survey.

Questions asked about the current year: 0. Questions asked about the building: 38.

Times the facilitators pointed to the correct assembly point on the map: 29. Assembly point now located inside a reservoir: 1.

Facilitators who suggested the colonist skip the fire-exit section: 0. Facilitators who suggested a revised map: 1, overruled.

Minutes of the final session spent standing on the hill in the lanyard: 25.

Certificates of completion awarded: 1.

The revival office said the colonist's first request on leaving was to see the building. "We told them it was the hill," the head facilitator said. "They asked which exit they were standing on."
drafts.premise: A mandatory 'Welcome Back' orientation is held for a colonist revived from cryosleep after nine hundred years, where facilitators spend six weeks on the lanyard, the icebreaker and the fire-exit map of a building that has since become a hill.

drafts.headline: Colony Beats Guidance, Mat Not Consulted
drafts.body:
Harrow Ledge's settlers reported on Friday that the continent-sized fungal mat beneath them grew 4 percent on the year, and the mat was not invited to hear it. The Quarterly Earnings Call ran forty minutes in the Ledge's grain hall. This is the final order of results read out.

Mat growth, year on year: 4.0 percent. Guidance: 3.1 percent. Exceeded.

Surface covered: 11.2 million square kilometres. Of this, the colony occupies 0.002 percent.

Spore-fall complaints from households: 212, down from 340.

Long-roots cut by the colony for building plank: 61 kilometres. Described as a one-off.

Long-roots cut by the mat from under the colony: none recorded.

Seats held by the mat on the Earnings Call: none.

Seats held by the mat on the Growth Panel, which sets the guidance: none.

Years the mat has been alive before landfall: not stated. Settlers' estimate of its age is under review by the Panel, which has no method.

Attendees who asked whether the mat was aware of the figures: one. The question was taken as a matter for next quarter.

Next call: three months from today, same hall, same agenda.

"We are very pleased with the result," said the Panel's speaker, Solveig Navarro. "The mat has been a steady performer for us."
drafts.premise: Colonists on a planet circling Tau Ceti hold a 'Quarterly Earnings Call' for their continent-sized fungal mat, reporting that it grew 4% year on year and 'exceeded guidance', while the mat, which has been alive since before landfall, is not asked to attend.

drafts.body:
The Gene-Editing Guild's card of apology reached the far hemisphere's only tardigrade-farmer on the 1,094th day of travel, ending the longest delivery in colony records. Results of the expedition follow.

Engineers who set out: 2,000

Engineers who arrived: 1,962

Engineers kept back at the Salt Divide to maintain the road home: 31

Engineers lost to the Divide: 7

Walking crawlers built to carry the card: 14

Crawlers that completed the trip: 3

Length of the farewell speech given by the expedition leader at the farmer's gate: 41 minutes

drafts.headline: Vault Opened For Bread
drafts.body:
The Founders' Vault was opened on Friday after eleven light-years and nine generations, and the first thing taken out was a sourdough starter. Results of the opening inventory follow. The vault holds 4,112,806 frozen genomes.

Human lines: 9,400
Livestock lines: 1,260
Orchard and grain lines: 38,775
Gut cultures: 212
Sourdough starters: 1
Sourdough starters matching the one the Lower Ovens have fed since landfall: 0
Sourdough starters matching the one the Upper Ovens have fed since landfall: 0
Bake-off judges who asked that the result be read twice: 3
Seals broken to reach the starter: 14
Seals remaining: 6,031
Openings of the vault the founders permitted: 1
Cost of the voyage, in ship-years of the fleet's yield: 211
Ship-years of yield the Ovens' dispute has cost the colony: not counted

The starter was grown out over four days under the eye of both ovens. Its loaves were judged blind at the Ledge hall. Both ovens placed it last. The Lower Ovens said it was too sour, and the Upper Ovens said it was too flat.

The genome notes show the original culture was a single strain. Both ovens' cultures have since drifted into several, and neither matches the founders'.

The bake-off will be held again in spring. The assembly's vault warden said the next opening would be for the cheese.
drafts.premise: A colony's founding genome vault, carried across eleven light-years at vast cost, is opened for the first time to retrieve the recipe for a sourdough starter, after a bake-off dispute that has run for nine generations.

quality.judge_reason: Its bureaucratic overkill (2,000 engineers, 212 at-home visits and zero knocks) skewers real institutional delivery failures, the spokesperson's kicker treats the absurdity as routine, and its opening doesn't give away the joke.
quality.critique: Sentences ran long and the list format buried the jokes, with few short punches. The headline described the premise, and the ending restated the cost line instead of turning it.

picture.reason: Image 2 shows the farmer holding the card at chest level in a plain shirt and trousers, not a patched coverall at arm's length, and its vehicles are wheeled cabs on a causeway rather than crawler machines spreading across the plain.
picture.winner_faults: The crawler machines carry garbled, illegible lettering, and the farmer's coverall shows no clear patches.
